feature: Making an arrow thicker takes one click
summary: Pick an arrow and its Thickness slider is right there, first row under the Arrow heading, beside its ending and head size. Until now the only way to it was a chevron on a row called Color, which said nothing about how thick a line is, so the commonest edit on a redline arrow was three moves down.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next. Nothing to switch on.

try.do: Press A for the arrow tool and drag an arrow across the canvas.
Press Escape to skip the caption field.
Drag the Thickness slider at the top of the Arrow section and watch the arrow get heavier.
Draw a rectangle and open the chevron on its Outline row in Appearance.
Move the Width slider in there and check the box's ring still follows it.
Shift click the arrow as well, so both are picked, and move that same Width slider.
Pick the arrow on its own again and confirm its Color row has no chevron to open.

evaluate: With an arrow picked, does your eye land on Thickness without hunting?
Is Thickness the word you would have gone looking for, or would you have expected Width, Weight or Size?
Does Thickness belong at the top of the Arrow section, above Caption and Ending, or somewhere else in that list?
With an arrow and a box picked together the one control is called Width and sits in the Outline part. Does that read as the same setting, or as two different ones?
Now that the arrow's Color row opens nothing, does the row still look clickable when it should not?
rough: The pictures are real screen captures from the loop's own probe app, taken with the Screen Recording grant.

The width has one home, never two. Where a shape's outline can be switched off (a box, an ellipse, a picture) it stays that part's Width in the drawer; where the line IS the shape (an arrow, a line) the part row loses its chevron and the width is the shape's own Thickness. Pick an arrow together with a box and the box wins, because they share a single row.
Considered putting a width control straight on the part row instead. That row is already a label, a switch and a colour, and a fourth control crowds it while leaving one word covering two things.
Found on the way and left alone: a highlight gets TWO rows in Appearance, both called Outline, one painting its stroke colour and one its border colour. Filed as its own task.
Corner Radius still shows under Effects for an arrow, where it does nothing. Not touched here.
